keyword: when was the last mission to the moon

verifications.claim: The last time humans went to the moon was during NASA's Apollo 17 mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Last time American on moon, Apollo 17" (R1); "The last time astronauts traveled that far was Apollo 17, in December 1972" (R2); "Apollo 17 — the final mission in the program, which was the last time humans traveled to the moon" (R3); "Apollo 17 became the last crewed mission to the Moon" (R4); "the last words spoken by a human on the moon" (R5); "Apollo 17 Post Mission Activities... last Apollo Moon landing flight" (R6); "the last humans to visit the Moon" (R7); "The last U.S. astronaut to land on the moon was on Dec. 19, 1972, during NASA's Apollo 17 mission" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: All references explicitly confirm Apollo 17 as the last human moon mission.

verifications.claim: NASA's Apollo 17 mission landed on December 11, 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Apollo 17 landed on the Moon in the valley of Taurus-Littrow on December 11, 1972.
verifications.reasoning: R7 directly states the exact landing date.

verifications.claim: NASA's Apollo 17 mission returned to Earth on December 19, 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "taking place between 7 and 19 December 1972" with splashdown (R4); "Dec. 19, 1972, splashdown" (R6); "splashed down... on December 19, 1972" (R7); "Dec. 19, 1972, during NASA's Apollo 17 mission" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly confirm the return/splashdown date.

verifications.claim: Astronauts Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt spent over three days on the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The Apollo 17 astronauts spent nearly 13 days in space — more than three of those on the lunar surface.
verifications.reasoning: R3 directly states Cernan and Schmitt (surface crew) spent more than three days on the surface.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 marks the final crewed lunar landing to date.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: See evidence for claim 1; all confirm final crewed landing.
verifications.reasoning: All references support Apollo 17 as the last crewed lunar landing.

verifications.claim: Eugene Cernan was the Mission Commander of Apollo 17.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "commander Gene Cernan" (R3); "Eugene Cernan as Mission Commander" (R4)

verifications.claim: Eugene Cernan was the last person to walk on the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Cernan was the last to leave the lunar surface" (R3, R4); "As he took his final steps before leaving the moon, Apollo 17 commander Gene Cernan" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: References confirm Cernan as last to leave/walk on moon.

verifications.claim: Harrison Schmitt was the Lunar Module Pilot of Apollo 17.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "lunar module pilot" (R3); "Harrison H. Schmitt was the lunar module pilot" (R4)

verifications.claim: Harrison Schmitt was the first trained geologist to visit the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the only Apollo mission to carry a trained geologist, Harrison H. Schmitt" (R4, R8)
verifications.reasoning: References state he was the (first) trained geologist on Apollo missions to moon.

verifications.claim: Ronald Evans was the Command Module Pilot of Apollo 17.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Ronald E. Evans as command module pilot

verifications.claim: The landing site of Apollo 17 was Taurus-Littrow valley.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.claim: Several uncrewed missions have landed on the moon since Apollo 17.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: References mention robotic missions (e.g., Chang'e) but none explicitly state several uncrewed landings post-Apollo 17.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 remains the last time humans walked on the moon's surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: All confirm no human moon walks since Apollo 17.

verifications.claim: NASA is currently working to return humans to the moon through the Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Artemis program details throughout, e.g., "NASA’s Artemis lunar program is the space agency's campaign to return American astronauts to the surface of the moon" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources describe Artemis as NASA's return program.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is slated to circle the moon in the near future.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Artemis II mission is to send a crew... around the moon" (R8); R2 full coverage of lunar flyby/circle mission.
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Artemis II as moon circling mission (recently executed in context).

verifications.claim: Artemis III is planned for a landing
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "Artemis 4... will be the first crewed Moon landing mission" (R4); "moon landing... Artemis IV" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: References specify Artemis IV (not III) as the planned landing mission, directly contradicting the claim.
